title: How blood is made, in 3D
question: How does a bone marrow stem cell become the cells in your blood?
representation: A native ManimGL 3D sequence: the trabecular lattice and marrow niche, stem-cell division, the three mature blood lineages, and their release into the circulation.

example.title: Inside a marrow niche
example.description: Bone struts, a red marrow pocket, dividing stem cells, and three cell lines leaving.

chapters.title: The marrow is a scaffold
chapters.question: What holds the marrow space open while blood cells are made?
chapters.insight: Bone is not a solid wall: a trabecular lattice frames the soft marrow.
chapters.safeguard: Do not present bone as a smooth shell; the open lattice is the point.
chapters.narration: Inside a bone, a beige lattice of trabeculae holds open a pocket of red marrow. The struts are rigid, but the space between them is soft and full of cells.

roles.struts: Trabeculae: rigid bone struts that frame the marrow pocket.
roles.marrow: Red marrow: the soft, well-supplied space where blood cells are produced.

cues.text: A bone is mostly empty space inside a lattice.
The red marrow sits in the pocket the struts protect.
The camera orbits while the structure holds still.

nodes.title: Trabeculae
nodes.body: Rigid bone struts that frame the marrow pocket instead of enclosing it.

nodes.title: Red marrow
nodes.body: The soft space between struts, supplied by blood and packed with stem cells.

visual.takeaway: The marrow is an open pocket held by a lattice, not a cavity in solid bone.

presentation.why: The learner needs to see the geometry of the niche before cells appear in it.
presentation.visualEvidence: Beige trabeculae surround and frame a translucent red marrow sphere in three dimensions.

continuity.bridge: Opening beat: establish the marrow niche in three dimensions.

chapters.title: One stem cell becomes many
chapters.question: How does one cell become the starting point for every blood lineage?
chapters.insight: Haematopoietic stem cells divide and commit to different fates.
chapters.safeguard: Division is not the same as specialisation; commitment follows it.
chapters.narration: With the lattice gone, the stem cells are visible. One divides, and the daughters begin to take different routes: some remain stem cells, others commit to a lineage.

roles.hsc: Haematopoietic stem cells: self-renewing cells that can commit to any blood lineage.
roles.daughter-a: Daughter cell A: a division product beginning to commit.
roles.daughter-b: Daughter cell B: a division product beginning to commit.

cues.text: The marrow clears and the stem cells are revealed.
One stem cell divides into two daughters.

nodes.title: Stem cell pool
nodes.body: A small group of haematopoietic stem cells in the marrow niche.

nodes.title: Division
nodes.body: One cell becomes two daughters that can take different fates.

visual.takeaway: Every blood cell starts from a stem cell that divided and then committed.

presentation.why: Division is a spatial event; seeing the daughter cells separate makes commitment legible.
presentation.visualEvidence: A stem cell splits into two daughters that move apart in the marrow space.

continuity.bridge: The niche is established; now watch the cells inside it divide.

chapters.title: Three cell lines enter the blood
chapters.question: What do committed blood cells become, and where do they go?
chapters.insight: Red cells, white cells and platelets leave the marrow for the circulation.
chapters.safeguard: Platelets are cell fragments, not whole cells; say so.
chapters.narration: The committed cells mature into the three lines that fill the blood: red cells that carry oxygen, white cells that defend the body, and platelets that seal leaks. Then they leave the marrow for the circulation.

roles.rbc: Red blood cell: a flexible disc packed with haemoglobin for oxygen transport.
roles.wbc: White blood cell: a nucleated defender of the tissue and blood.
roles.plts: Platelets: small cell fragments that clump to seal a vessel.

cues.text: Three mature cell types appear around the niche.
Each rotates so its shape is visible.
The mature cells move out into the circulation.
Blood is built cell by cell, continuously.

nodes.title: Red cell
nodes.body: A biconcave, haemoglobin-filled disc that carries oxygen.

nodes.title: White cell
nodes.body: A nucleated cell that patrols tissue and blood for threats.

nodes.title: Platelets
nodes.body: Small cell fragments that stick to damaged vessel walls.

visual.takeaway: One stem-cell source supplies oxygen, immunity and clotting for a lifetime.

presentation.why: The three lineages must be compared by shape and colour at the same moment.
presentation.visualEvidence: A red disc, a lobed white cell and yellow platelets rotate side by side.

continuity.bridge: The daughters have committed; now see what they become.
